mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes V Class V250d or V300d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A V250d or V300d engine replacement typically costs between £3,100 and £5,900 depending on engine code (OM651.921, OM651.941, OM654.910 or OM654.920), condition type, and whether fitting is included. Rebuilt OM651.921 (V250d, 2014-2019): £3,100-£4,900 supply only. Rebuilt OM651.941 (V300d, 2014-2019): £3,300-£5,200 supply only. Rebuilt OM654.910 (V250d, 2019-2024): £3,200-£5,400 supply only. Rebuilt OM654.920 (V300d, 2019-2024): £3,500-£5,900 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £1,800-£4,500 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What causes the OM651 timing chain rattle on cold start in a V250d or V300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651 timing chain rattle is caused by tensioner failure allowing oil pressure loss, leading to chain stretch and guide wear. The chain tensioner has been revised multiple times, primarily affecting older OM651 engines. The chain is at the rear of the engine - most repairs require engine removal. Early W447 models (2014-2016) are most vulnerable to timing chain issues. Cold-start rattling indicates chain elongation requiring full engine-out replacement. Rebuilt OM651 units include updated tensioner seals and hardened guide rails as standard. The OM651's single most critical failure point is the timing chain system.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM654 EGR cooler failure on a facelift V250d or V300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM654's EGR cooler typically shows warning signs before complete failure. Loss of power and rough idle. Increased fuel consumption. Coolant loss with no visible external leak. Emissions warning lights illuminated. White smoke from the exhaust.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my V250d or V300d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner on OM651, EGR cooler on OM654, HPFP). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing chain failure. OM651 timing chain replacement: £1,200-£1,800 - do this if rattle is persistent. OM654 EGR cooler replacement: £950-£1,350 - catch it early. Full OM651 rebuild: £3,500-£5,200 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Full OM654 rebuild: £3,500-£5,500 - for catastrophic failure or 100k+ miles. Given V Class V250d / V300d values (£18,000-£40,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my V250d or V300d has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on a machined flat on the engine block - on OM651, front of the block on the driver's side. V250d (2014-2019): OM651.921 (2.1L diesel, 204hp). V300d (2014-2019): OM651.941 (2.1L diesel, 240hp). V250d (2019-2024): OM654.910 (2.0L diesel, 190hp). V300d (2019-2024): OM654.920 (2.0L diesel, 237hp).

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used V250d or V300d engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a V Class diesel. The W447 engine bay layout, 7G-TRONIC or 9G-TRONIC gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Engine removal requires proper lifting equipment and subframe lowering. ECU coding and injector calibration require Mercedes-Benz Star Diagnosis tools. AdBlue system recalibration needed on Euro 6 models. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,500 - worth every penny.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes V Class V250d / V300d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes V Class V250d and V300d are powered by two of Mercedes' most capable diesel engines - the OM651 2.1-litre twin-turbo and the OM654 2.0-litre modular diesel. While both offer impressive performance and refinement, they have developed well-documented reputations for specific failures. Timing chain tensioner wear dominates OM651 replacement demand, while OM654 EGR cooler crystallisation and high-pressure fuel pump issues drive repair enquiries on facelift models. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common V250d and V300d engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the V250d / V300d Rattles on Cold Start
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes V Class V250d (OM651.921) and V300d (OM651.941), 2014-2019
problems.rootCause: The OM651's single most critical failure point is the timing chain system. A faulty tensioner allows oil pressure loss, causing chain slack and a characteristic rattle on cold start. The chain stretches and guides wear over time. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, leading to catastrophic valve and piston interference. The chain tensioner has been revised multiple times, primarily affecting older OM651 engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner and seal only - engine-in-situ
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught very early with no chain stretch

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine-out replacement of chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Required if rattle is persistent or chain has stretched

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with upgraded tensioner, new timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped or guides have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W447 V Class V250d or V300d is worth £18,000-£40,000 depending on age and mileage - the full replacement cost of £3,500-£5,200 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £12,000, evaluate repair options carefully.
problems.recommendation: If you are hearing a metallic rattle at cold start on a V250d or V300d under 90,000 miles, a preventative timing chain replacement is the most cost-effective route. However, if the chain has already jumped timing or damaged the cylinder head, a full rebuilt OM651 engine is the only financially sensible option to avoid repeated downtime and costly collateral repairs.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 engine prices for your Mercedes V250d / V300d

problems.h4: OM654 EGR Cooler Crystallisation - Why the Facelift V250d / V300d Loses Power
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes V Class V250d (OM654.910) and V300d (OM654.920), 2019-2024
problems.rootCause: The OM654's EGR cooler can suffer from crystallisation and carbon buildup, particularly on vehicles used for short journeys. This leads to reduced performance, rough idle, increased fuel consumption, and emissions warning lights. Coolant loss without a visible external leak may indicate a cracked or internally leaking EGR cooler.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR cooler, clear carbon deposits, reset adaptations
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative; suitable for minor carbon buildup

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler with updated design, clean EGR valve, reset adaptions
repairOptions.longevity: Required if crystallisation has caused permanent blockage or coolant loss

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM654 with new EGR components, emissions system calibrated, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary if coolant ingress has caused cylinder damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a V Class V250d or V300d worth £18,000-£40,000, EGR cooler replacement at £950-£1,350 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified if emissions system failure has caused secondary damage.
problems.recommendation: On a facelift V250d or V300d used primarily for airport transfers or motorway cruising, EGR systems clog less frequently. However, if your vehicle operates in heavy city traffic, an EGR cooler replacement is a practical mid-term fix. If the crack has allowed coolant into the combustion chamber, a full rebuilt engine is strongly advised to prevent catastrophic cylinder scoring.
problems.cta: -> Compare OM654 EGR repair costs for your V250d / V300d

problems.group: OM651 / OM654 High-Pressure Fuel Pump & Injector Issues
problems.h4: OM651 / OM654 High-Pressure Fuel Pump & Injector Issues - Fuel System Failures
problems.rootCause: High-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) wear and injector seal degradation are documented issues across both OM651 and OM654 families. Fuel system failures can cause hard starting, rough idle, and in severe cases, complete engine failure if metal debris contaminates the fuel system.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace injector copper seals, clean injector bores, oil change
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before ring damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace high-pressure fuel pump, flush fuel system, replace filter
repairOptions.longevity: Required if HPFP wear has been detected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete supply & fit with new HPFP, injectors, updated seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Guaranteed resolution; eliminates hidden fuel system contamination

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a V Class V250d or V300d worth £18,000-£40,000, HPFP replacement at £700-£1,200 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified if fuel system debris has caused bottom-end damage.
problems.recommendation: We recommend a full reconditioned engine if fuel dilution of the oil is detected or if metal debris has contaminated the fuel system. Partial fixes on a compromised fuel system rarely survive commercial delivery cycles, making a complete rebuilt unit the most cost-effective long-term investment for fleet operators.
